clues: This chief town sits near the very heart of South America. Wide farm lands and cow lands stretch out all round its streets and homes.
From May to the fall, a mass of dry air sits over the land and holds back the rain. Then the wet months roll in and the rain comes hard.
Gold fever gave birth to this town in the year 1719. Men rushed in to dig for gold and stayed on to trade with farms.
In 2014 the world came here for the World Cup of soccer. Games of that cup filled its big ground, the largest in the state.
This town is known far and wide as the south gate to the Amazon. That name marks the way in to the great green wild lands.
